scenes.text: You paste your salary slip into a chatbot, and ask it to plan your taxes. [1] Where does that data go? Who can see it? Could it be used for training? [2] Let's talk about AI and your privacy.

Here's what happens when you send a message. [1] Your text travels, encrypted, to the company's servers. [2] The model reads it, and writes a reply. [3] The chat may be stored, for your history and for safety checks. [4] Depending on the settings, it may be used to train future models. [5] And it's deleted after a set time, or when you delete it.

There are two very different setups. [1] Consumer chat apps, where your chats may be used to improve models, unless you opt out. [2] Business and API plans, which usually don't train on your data by default, and come with contracts.

So what should you never paste into a public chatbot? [1] Passwords, and OTPs. [2] Full ID numbers, like Aadhaar, PAN, or bank details. [3] And confidential work data, like client files, or unreleased code.

Here are smart privacy habits. [1] Turn off training on your chats, in the app's settings. [2] Remove names and numbers, before pasting documents. [3] And for sensitive work, use a business plan, or run a model locally, from episode 38.

Here are four terms. [1] Personal data, anything that identifies you. [2] Data retention, how long your chats are kept. [3] Opt out, choosing not to let your data be used for training. [4] And India's DPDP Act, the Digital Personal Data Protection law, which gives you rights over your data.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think deleting a chat from the screen removes it everywhere, instantly. [2] Companies may keep it for a while, for safety and legal reasons. Read the privacy policy, and share carefully from the start.

data.myth: Deleting a chat removes it everywhere, instantly.
data.fact: Companies may keep it for a while for safety and legal reasons. Share carefully from the start.
